proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is a kind of legal right (ius) in Roman property law — specifically the right to alienate, consume, or destroy the thing owned. It is externally grounded in a legal system's recognition of ownership relations, not in any intrinsic physical property of the bearer or the res. This makes it a Role (BFO_0000023), a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (the dominus) and is conferred by a socio-legal structure. It is further a subtype of the existing working:LegalRight class, which is already typed as BFO_0000023. Abusus is a kind (class) rather than an individual, since it is a general legal category instantiated by many particular right-bearers.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a specific type of legal right within Roman property theory; LegalRight (BFO_0000023) is the existing working-ontology class capturing such roles, so Abusus is appropriately a subclass of it.

open_questions: Should Abusus be distinguished from Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right to fruits) as sibling subclasses of LegalRight, so that the full dominium triad is represented? If so, should we also mint working:Usus and working:Fructus now?

Is Abusus being considered here as a purely Roman-law historical category (in which case it is a class whose instances are historically bound roles), or as a general jurisprudential concept that recurs in civil-law systems (e.g., French Code Civil Art. 544)? This affects whether the class should carry a temporal or jurisdictional scope restriction.

Abusus inheres in the owner (dominus) qua owner. Should we also represent the class of bearers (e.g., a Dominus or PropertyOwner role) and assert that instances of Abusus inhere in bearers of that role, using RO_0000052?

Roman law treats Abusus as part of the bundle constituting full dominium. Should we model dominium as a complex role or as a collection (aggregate) of Usus, Fructus, and Abusus roles, possibly using BFO_0000051 (has part)?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus, the Roman-law ius abutendi, is the power of the owner to alienate, consume, or destroy the object of ownership. In BFO 2020 terms it is a specifically dependent continuant (BFO_0000020) of the Role subtype (BFO_0000023): it does not inhere in the physical object by virtue of any intrinsic property, but is conferred on a bearer — the dominus — by the legal-institutional structure that recognises ownership. It is therefore parallel in structure to working:LegalRight, which is already modelled as BFO_0000023, and Abusus is naturally a subclass of that class. It is typed as a class (not an individual) because it is a general jurisprudential kind instantiated by every individual bearer of the right in every relevant legal system. The core relation proposed is rdfs:subClassOf working:LegalRight. Several open questions remain about the full modelling of the dominium bundle and cross-jurisdictional scope.
